title: litellm 1.107.0 on PyPI: credential stealer and persistent backdoor

packages.name: litellm
packages.note: Only 1.107.0 is reported malicious; 1.106.2, 1.107.0rc1 and 1.107.0rc2 are reported clean.

files.name: cook.pth
files.note: Runs 'import cook' at every Python start.

files.name: sitecustomize.py
files.note: Starts a detached hourly backdoor daemon.

remediation: Delete cook.pth, cook.py and sitecustomize.py from the listed site-packages directories, then uninstall litellm==1.107.0 and pin 1.106.2 or a later verified release.
Kill any detached python process with parent PID 1 and working directory '/' that you did not start, and remove the /tmp artifacts listed above.
Treat every host that installed 1.107.0 as compromised: rotate the credentials in the checklist below, and review cloud audit logs for use of those credentials.
Block outbound access to www.litellm.dev and search DNS/proxy logs for it.
A host that ran the backdoor before the package was pulled (~13:40 UTC) may have executed second-stage code; investigate it as a full compromise.
caveats: IOCs were transcribed from the SafeDep write-up on 2026-10-21 and have not been independently verified against the malicious wheels. Re-check hashes against the original article before acting on a CONFIRMED/COMPROMISED verdict, and update this feed as the investigation evolves.
Install timestamps come from filesystem birth/modification time and can be wrong if environments were copied, restored or built by tools that preserve timestamps.
